original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The category $\QCoh(S_\etale, \mathcal{O})$
of quasi-coherent modules on $S_\etale$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is of finite presentation.
then the internal hom
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

final_content.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\operatorname{QCoh}(S_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\mathcal O)$ denote quasi-coherent modules on its small étale ringed site. This category has the following closure properties (where exactness, colimits and internal Hom are taken in the ambient category of site modules): (1) arbitrary direct sums and (2) arbitrary colimits are quasi-coherent; (3) kernels and cokernels of morphisms between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (4) in a short exact sequence of site modules, if any two of the three terms are quasi-coherent, so is the third; (5) tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (6) if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, then $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is quasi-coherent.
hypotheses: Quasi-coherent modules on the small étale ringed site of a scheme.
conclusions: Listed closure properties for sums, colimits, kernels/cokernels, extensions, tensor products and finite-presentation internal Hom.

\label{lemma-qc-colimits}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
has colimits and they agree with colimits in the categories
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, and
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
the tensor products $\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{G}$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
with $\mathcal{F}$ finite locally free (in fppf, or equivalently \'etale, or
equivalently Zariski topology) the internal homs
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

final_content.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme. For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ consider the big ringed site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ and its associated category of $\mathcal O$-modules; identify a quasi-coherent module on each site by the common pullback-section rule $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,f^*\mathcal F_S)$ from a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. (1) The category $\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}},\mathcal O)$ has all colimits; their images under each of the three associated-site inclusions agree with the ambient module-category colimits. (2) For any two such quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, their tensor products computed in the big Zariski, étale and fppf module categories agree and are quasi-coherent. (3) If additionally $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free (equivalently for the Zariski, étale and fppf topologies), then the internal Hom sheaves $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ computed in these three big site module categories agree and are quasi-coherent.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; F,G are quasi-coherent big-fppf modules; finite locally free F for part 3.
conclusions: Colimits, tensors and (with finite-locally-free source) internal Homs are computed compatibly across the three big sites.
